title: The Whispering Manor
premise: A letter from a frightened apprentice calls you to Vask Manor, where the inventor Ottoline Vask vanished while chasing a phenomenon called the Echo.
introLines: The letter arrived on a night without wind. It asked for one thing: finish what Ottoline Vask began.
Vask Manor waits on the hill. The gate opens before you knock.
Somewhere inside, a voice repeats your footsteps a heartbeat late.

characters.name: Tallow
characters.voice: Courteous and dry. Careful, old-fashioned sentences.

characters.name: Ottoline Vask
characters.voice: Brisk, curious and warm. Teases herself in her notes.

characters.name: Wren Dabney
characters.voice: Anxious and honest. Short, breathless lines.

characters.name: Edric Maul
characters.voice: Silky and patient. Every kindness has a price.

characters.name: The Echo
characters.voice: Repeats the last words it hears, bent a little each time.

endings.title: Release the Echo
epilogue: The final ring opens. Pale voices rise like moths through the vault roof, carrying their grief into the morning.
Ottoline's last memory thanks you. It is a farewell, not a return. You let it go.
By sunrise the manor is silent. Wren and Tallow walk out beside you, and the wind has no borrowed voice.

endings.title: Become the Echo's Guardian
epilogue: You set the binding key down and offer an open hand. The Echo answers in its own voice, no longer borrowing Ottoline's.
You stay by choice, and it stays by choice. Together you tend the memories without making them a prison.
Wren brings letters from the world outside. Tallow lights a second lantern at the gate. The manor becomes a home for those who need to be heard.

endings.title: Seal the Echo
epilogue: One by one, the containment rings lock around a steady silver light. The Echo is sheltered, and its reach no longer spills into the world.
You leave no throne in the vault. The seal belongs to no investor and answers to no master.
Wren records the bindings so that one day they may be opened safely. Behind the glass, a voice sings a song only it remembers.

journalEntries.title: Wren's request
journalEntries.text: Wren asked me to find what became of Ottoline. The letter fixes her disappearance at twenty to midnight.

journalEntries.title: Ottoline's research
journalEntries.text: Ottoline hid her notes in ciphers and treated the Echo as a guest. Her journal links memory, water, fire and wind.

journalEntries.title: The investor signed in
journalEntries.text: E. Maul signed the visitor ledger before the accident. His presence was no coincidence.

journalEntries.title: A voice preserved in wax
journalEntries.text: The recording proves Ottoline knew the engine might fail. Water must wake first; the tuner remembers 73.

journalEntries.title: The hour of the accident
journalEntries.text: The clock remembers 11:40, exactly as Wren wrote. Its case held the missing resonance core.

journalEntries.title: The keeper witnessed the aftermath
journalEntries.text: The keeper heard wind close the circle. The engine was following a pattern when someone interfered.

text.base: Tallow offered his lantern even when I would not listen. Kindness is his choice, not a reward I can demand.

variants.text: Tallow trusted me with his locket. Ottoline asked him to protect people, not machinery.

text.base: I treated the Echo as an instrument. It remembered that demand.

variants.text: I promised to listen without ownership. The Echo offered guardianship only if we both choose it.

text.base: I rejected Maul's ownership. Ottoline's alchemy and star charts may still reveal safe containment.

variants.text: I learned the containment words. They can seal the Echo, but cannot restore Ottoline's life.

journalEntries.title: The pressed lilac
journalEntries.text: The seal opens on Ottoline's pressed lilac. Her note reads: 'Wren stayed to help me. He did not abandon us.'

journalEntries.title: Ottoline's chosen path
journalEntries.text: Starlight draws Ottoline's route through the vault. She entered willingly to bring the lost voices home.

journalEntries.title: A child learning to remember
journalEntries.text: The tablet reveals a lesson: 'The Echo learns by repetition, as a child does. It is neither demon nor machine.'

journalEntries.title: The stabilizer was sabotaged
journalEntries.text: A silver memory forms in the retort: Maul replaced the stabilizer before the accident. Ottoline's formula was sound.

journalEntries.title: Maul's mark
journalEntries.text: The mirror clears. Wren's reflection points at Maul's signet scratched into the damaged stabilizer.

journalEntries.title: The accident reconstructed
journalEntries.text: The completed timeline proves Maul caused the failure before Ottoline vanished. Wren's testimony is corroborated.

journalEntries.title: Ottoline's last request
journalEntries.text: The matching call releases Ottoline's last message: 'The Echo remembers kindness. Ask what it wants; never command it to become me.'

text.base: The restored engine waits. The Echo must be released, contained, or guarded by mutual consent.

variants.text: I released the Echo and let the memories go. Freedom required a farewell.
I sealed the Echo without claiming it. The world is safe while Wren safeguards the bindings.
I became its guardian. We chose to keep watch together without ownership.

evidenceLinks.label: Two independent accounts fix the accident at 11:40.
The visitor's name matches the signet on the damaged stabilizer.
The mark and the recovered formula point to deliberate sabotage.
The timeline confirms the cut preceded the alarm and disappearance.
The Echo learns and chooses; it is more than an instrument.
Star alignment and alchemical stability reconstruct safe containment.
Ottoline's last request corroborates the Echo's need for consent.
Water opens the sequence; wind closes it.
